title: (RHBA-2008:0046) gnome-screensaver bug fix update
portal_summary: An updated gnome-screensaver package that fixes various bugs is now available.

portal_solution:
Before applying this update, make sure that all previously-released errata
relevant to your system have been applied.

This update is available via Red Hat Network. Details on how to use the Red
Hat Network to apply this update are available at
http://kbase.redhat.com/faq/FAQ_58_10188
portal_description:
The gnome-screensaver package contains the GNOME project's official
screensaver program. It is designed for improved integration with a GNOME
desktop, including themeability, language support, and Human Interface
Guidelines (HIG) compliance. It also provides screen-locking and fast
user-switching from a locked screen.

This update addresses the following issues:

* gnome-screensaver was not able to nicely fade-out when locking the
screen, providing no warning that the screen was going to be locked. This
has been fixed so that gnome-screensaver now fades out properly before
locking the screen.

* pressing ctrl-alt--keypad-slash would deactivate the X server's keyboard 
grabs, which was sufficient to circumvent the screen-locking mechanism used
by gnome-screensaver. This has been disabled and a debugging option added
to the Xorg configuration file, /etc/X11/xorg.conf, which allows the
reactivation of the X server's keyboard grabs. To enable this behavior, the
following line must now be listed in the "Server Layout" section of xorg.conf:

	Option "AllowDeactivateGrabs"

* pressing ctrl+alt+keypad-multiply would kill clients with an active
keyboard or mouse grab as well as killing any application that may have 
locked the server, which was sufficient to circumvent the screen-locking
mechanism used by gnome-screensaver. This has been disabled and a debugging
option added to the Xorg configuration file, /etc/X11/xorg.conf, which
allows the reactivation of the X server's keyboard grabs. To enable this
behavior, the following line must now be listed in "ServerLayout" section
of xorg.conf:

	Option "AllowClosedownGrabs"

Users of gnome-screensaver should upgrade to this updated package, which
resolves these issues.
